newsitem.title: UK: Sabre buys Rudolf Wolff fund management team.
newsitem.headline: Sabre buys Rudolf Wolff fund management team.

text.p: Sabre Fund Management Ltd and Rudolf Wolff and Co Ltd said on Thursday that they have signed a memorandum of understanding under which Wolff's fund management operation will be sold to Sabre.
Rudolf Wolff is a ring-dealing member of the London Metal Exchange (LME) and is a subsidiary of Canadian metal producer Noranda Inc.
Its funds are administered by an in-house accounting team in Dublin. The business was founded by Wolff in 1986 and has around $150 million under management at present.

"We decided to broaden our product range by developing expertise in manager selection. Buying a company which has that skill is clearly preferable, since the team is proven and experienced," Sabre Chairman Colin Barrow.
Sabre is a London-based investment management group, which was founded in 1982. It applies active investment strategies, particularly the technical analysis of of derivatives markets.
"We are delighted that they (Wolff) are coming on board. There are excellent synergies between the two groups and we now have an excellent skill-set," said Robin Edwards, Director at Sabre.
Sabre sees enormous potential in the absolute performance industry in such areas as hedge funds. "This will be the first of many acquisitions we will make," Edwards said.
Sabre's purchase of Wolff's fund management operation is the first example of this programme of expansion. The unit will be known as Sabre Wolff.
